china-1924-5:p0796_1.rationale: Continuation of the monthly central government expense list: the special-area prisons item and the Ministry of Justice total. This is public expenditure by item.

china-1924-5:p0796_2.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Education, covering its colleges, schools, student funds abroad and subsidies, with a total. It is both a central budget item and education funding.

china-1924-5:p0796_3.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce and its stations and bureaus. Primarily a central government expenditure list.

china-1924-5:p0796_4.rationale: Ministry of Communications monthly expense, consisting solely of the Vladivostok railway supervision association. It is a budget line.

china-1924-5:p0796_5.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Bureau for Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs, including its school and allowances to princes. It is a central government expenditure list.

china-1924-5:p0797_1.rationale: Remaining central government monthly expense items (Mongolian and Tibetan bureau, imperial pensions) and the grand total of fifteen sections. It is budget expenditure.
review_questions: Is a tag for imperial pensions needed? Existing tags only partly fit, and imperial-household is not clearly about pension finance.

china-1924-5:p0797_2.rationale: Surplus of maritime and native customs revenue for 1921, in taels, available to meet the government deficit.

china-1924-5:p0797_3.rationale: Salt surplus released, revenue detained by the provinces and special items paid from the surplus, October 1921 to September 1922. It concerns the fiscal salt revenue.

china-1924-5:p0798_1.rationale: Collections of the Peking octroi and their earmarked monthly funds (notes redemption, schools, judiciary reform, students in Japan). The octroi is a local levy and the table shows how its revenue is allocated.
review_questions: Is a tag for octroi or local levies needed?

china-1924-5:p0798_2.rationale: Amounts of mining, stamp, wine and tobacco, and income taxes and government property profits actually received by the central government.
